content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished bookmark manager with:

- Add, edit, delete, favorite, archive, and restore
- Search, tag filters, collections, and sorting
- Grid and list layouts
- Local browser persistence
- Responsive mobile design
- Keyboard shortcuts: `N` to add, `⌘/Ctrl + K` to search

The app is ready at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This is looking really nice — clean, and I can see the everyday things I'd want: adding, editing, deleting, tagging, searching, sorting, and keeping links in collections. The archive-vs-delete distinction works the way I'd hope too.

Two things are getting in the way of how I'd actually use it, though:

1. **Saving a link is more manual than I expected.** When I paste a URL, I have to type the title (and description) myself — the form even requires a title before it'll save. What I really want is: I drop in a link and the app pulls in the page's title and description on its own, and then I can tweak them if I like. That auto-fill is honestly the main reason I'd use an app like this instead of just jotting links down.

2. **There's no "read later" / unread.** I can favorite things, but favoriting isn't the same as flagging something I haven't gotten to yet and want to come back to. I'd want to mark a bookmark as unread and then see just my unread ones in their own view, and clear them once I've read them.

Could you take another pass at those two? The rest of what you've shown feels solid for what I need.

content:
Implemented both improvements:

- Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its page title and description.
- Metadata remains editable before saving.
- Title is no longer required; the domain is used as a fallback.
- New bookmarks default to unread.
- Added a dedicated Unread view with a live count.
- Each card now has a one-click Read/Unread toggle.
- Unread status is preserved when editing and stored locally.

Verified metadata retrieval against a live public page. The updated app is available at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This is exactly what I was after. I pasted a link and it pulled in the title on its own, and I could still change it before saving — that's the effortless save I wanted. And the read-later side works the way I pictured: new links start as unread, there's an Unread view with a running count, and I can flip something to read (or back) in one tap.

Both of the things I raised are handled, and everything else I saw before still holds up. This does what I need to save and manage my bookmarks. I'm happy with it.
